answer:
IDENTIFICATION: The variable is RACE (SAMPLE_RACE) — specifically the Black vs. White contrast. Its log-odds coefficient on BA degree completion collapses to ≈0.09 and loses statistical significance once SES and the academic characteristics (ABILITY + PERCENTILE IN CLASS) are added, which is exactly the 0.5024→0.0923 / becomes-insignificant pattern described. This shows the Black–White gap in BA completion is largely mediated by SES and academic performance rather than race per se.

REFERENCE CATEGORIES (confirmed): SAMPLE_RACE uses White as reference (dummies BLACK, HISPANIC); SAMPLE_SEX uses Female as reference (dummy MALE). Adjusted models use White and Female references as required.

CONVERGENCE/SEPARATION: All 9 Logit models converged (converged=True), no separation warnings, no perfect-separation flags, despite the 2.7% base rate (236/8773). Standard errors are well-behaved.

=== CORRELATION / MEAN-DIFFERENCE TABLE (candidate vs blocks) ===
FAMILY SIZE (continuous): r(SES)=+0.024, r(ABILITY)=−0.242, r(PERCENTILE)=−0.154, r(BA)=−0.139.
SAMPLE_RACE — mean of blocks by category:
  White    n=5337  SES=+0.180  ABILITY=2065.5  PERCENTILE=51.71  BA_rate=0.0354
  Black    n=2113  SES=−0.210  ABILITY=1725.2  PERCENTILE=39.76  BA_rate=0.0133
  Hispanic n=1323  SES=−0.451  ABILITY=1824.7  PERCENTILE=40.85  BA_rate=0.0144
SAMPLE_SEX:
  Female   n=4437  SES=−0.026  ABILITY=1936.0  PERCENTILE=50.25  BA_rate=0.0295
  Male     n=4336  SES=+0.008  ABILITY=1958.7  PERCENTILE=44.07  BA_rate=0.0242
Interpretation: RACE is the candidate most strongly tied to SES and academic performance (Black/Hispanic groups have markedly lower SES, lower ability, lower class percentile, and lower BA rates), so its raw effect is the one most plausibly mediated/absorbed by the SES+academic blocks.

=== COEFFICIENT TABLE (log-odds; unadjusted vs adjusted=candidate+SES+ABILITY+PERCENTILE) ===
FAMILY SIZE (continuous), unstandardized:
  unadj: coef=−0.5077 se=0.0408 p=1.6e-35  |  adj: coef=−0.5085 se=0.0478 p=2.0e-26  (NO attenuation, stays significant)
FAMILY SIZE, standardized:
  unadj_z: −1.1317 (p=1.6e-35) | adj_z: −1.1336 (p=2.0e-26)
SAMPLE_SEX (MALE, Female ref):
  unadj: −0.2037 se=0.1328 p=0.125 | adj: −0.2235 se=0.1410 p=0.113  (insignificant both ways; no big drop)
SAMPLE_RACE (White ref):
  BLACK    unadj: −1.0057 se=0.2042 p=8.4e-07 (significant) | adj: +0.0926 se=0.2246 p=0.6801 (INSIGNIFICANT)
  HISPANIC unadj: −0.9241 se=0.2427 p=1.4e-04 (significant) | adj: −0.2665 se=0.2539 p=0.2939 (insignificant)

MATCH TO 0.5024 / 0.0923: The adjusted BLACK coefficient = 0.0926 with p=0.68 (insignificant) reproduces the "0.0923, becomes insignificant" endpoint essentially exactly. The variable is therefore RACE (Black vs White).

CAVEAT ON THE 0.5024 STARTING VALUE: In this processed dataset the unadjusted Black (White-ref) coefficient is −1.0057 (Hispanic-ref −0.8757), not +0.5024; no standard coding of the race dummies (White/Female refs, standardized dummies, 2-way collapse, OLS-LPM) reproduces +0.5024. Notably FAMILY SIZE happens to have an unadjusted magnitude ≈0.51 (−0.5077) but it does NOT attenuate (stays −0.5085, p~1e-26), so it cannot be the described variable. I therefore treat the exact 0.5024 figure as likely originating from the source study's original sample/coding (or a standardized/marginal quantity) that differs slightly from this processed CSV; the variable identification is nonetheless unambiguous from the 0.0923 adjusted match plus the loss of significance, and is consistent with the mediation story (race → SES/ability → BA).

payload.hypothesis: The effect of RACE (SAMPLE_RACE) — specifically the Black vs. White contrast — on BA degree completion decreases from a large, statistically significant unadjusted coefficient to ≈0.09 (log-odds, p≈0.68, insignificant) once both SES and the academic characteristics (ABILITY composite test score and PERCENTILE IN CLASS) are included. The Black–White racial gap in BA completion is therefore largely explained by (mediated through) differences in socioeconomic status and academic performance rather than by race itself.
payload.workflow: Loaded data/nls_ses_processed.csv (8773 rows, dropped redundant index column), verified no missing values and 2.7% BA-completion base rate. Computed candidate-vs-block correlations (FAMILY SIZE) and mean differences of SES/ABILITY/PERCENTILE across SAMPLE_RACE and SAMPLE_SEX categories. Fit logistic regression (statsmodels.Logit) for each demographic candidate: unadjusted (candidate only) and adjusted (candidate + SES + ABILITY + PERCENTILE IN CLASS), with White (race) and Female (sex) as reference categories, reporting coefficient, SE, and Wald p-value on both unstandardized and standardized scales. All models converged with no separation warnings. Matched the 0.0923/insignificant signature to the adjusted BLACK racial dummy (0.0926, p=0.6801).
